agenda: The situation in the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela
members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Russian Federation’s objectives are to prevent any resolution from legitimizing external intervention or regime change, to preserve language on sovereignty and non-interference, and to channel the Council toward dialogue and humanitarian access with the consent of Venezuelan authorities. The main difficulty will be avoiding a veto from the United States, France or the United Kingdom while retaining enough support among elected members; the text therefore avoids naming either Maduro or Guaidó and focuses on a neutral humanitarian and dialogue approach that can attract at least nine votes.

messages.Belgium: Belgium cannot support this draft as it stands: it is silent on free and fair presidential elections and on the legitimate role of the democratically elected National Assembly, and its humanitarian-access language risks giving the de facto authorities a veto over assistance. We ask the penholder to add clear language on elections and to guarantee unhindered access across all borders through impartial humanitarian actors. We also call for explicit condemnation of violence against protesters and humanitarian workers.
messages.China: China supports the Russian draft as a balanced basis for the Council’s consideration. It already reflects principles China considers essential: sovereignty, non-interference, peaceful dialogue and the consent and coordination of the affected State for humanitarian assistance. China therefore supports the text as it stands and does not request amendments at this stage. We would oppose any effort to introduce language that recognizes parallel authorities or authorizes external action.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d'Ivoire supports the draft's emphasis on sovereignty, non-interference and peaceful dialogue, and we thank the Russian Federation for its efforts. We ask that the text explicitly include free, fair and credible elections as part of the Venezuelan-led solution, and that humanitarian access be specified as including across borders and lines of conflict. These adjustments would strengthen the Council's message and help ensure aid reaches those in need. We can support the text with these changes.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic thanks the Russian Federation for this balanced draft. We support the text as it stands, as it upholds sovereignty, non-interference, and the need for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led dialogue, while calling for unhindered humanitarian access. We urge all Council members to support this effort to speak with one voice.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the Russian draft as presented. It reflects our core concerns on sovereignty, non-interference and a Venezuelan-led political solution. We particularly value the emphasis on consent and coordination with Venezuelan authorities for humanitarian access. We therefore do not request changes at this stage.
messages.France: France cannot support the draft as it stands. We need a clear call for free, fair and credible presidential elections, and humanitarian access must not be conditioned on the consent of the de facto authorities. We also ask that the text recognize the International Contact Group's efforts alongside the Montevideo Mechanism. With these changes, France could engage constructively.
messages.Germany: Germany cannot support the Russian draft as it stands: it would effectively make the Maduro authorities the gatekeepers for humanitarian aid and omits the need for free and fair presidential elections. We ask the penholder to amend PP6 and OP5 to guarantee unhindered humanitarian access, and OP4 to set a clear path to credible elections with international observation. We also expect the Council to condemn the excessive use of force against peaceful protesters and to call for respect for human rights and the release of political prisoners. Without these changes, Germany will not be in a position to support the text.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the draft as a balanced and viable basis for the Council’s response. It reflects the principles of sovereignty, non-interference, peaceful settlement and inclusive dialogue, while calling for humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles and in coordination with the Venezuelan authorities. We therefore encourage all members to support the text as it stands.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait supports the draft's reaffirmation of sovereignty, non-interference and the need for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led dialogue. To be able to support the text, we ask that OP4 explicitly include the National Assembly and all constitutional institutions, that OP5 ensure humanitarian access across land borders and without political preconditions, and that a new operative paragraph call for free, fair and transparent presidential elections in accordance with Venezuela's Constitution. If these balance and humanitarian elements are not reflected, Kuwait may abstain.
messages.Peru: Peru cannot support the draft as written because it treats the Maduro regime as the relevant authority and conditions humanitarian access on its consent, while failing to recognize the legitimate interim presidency of Juan Guaidó and the National Assembly. We ask for a new operative paragraph recognizing Guaidó and the National Assembly and calling for free and fair elections, and for OP5 to demand unhindered humanitarian access without political or military impediments. We also seek condemnation of violence by Venezuelan security forces and a broader reference to regional efforts, including the Lima Group.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot support the Russian draft as it stands: it treats the Maduro authorities as the legitimate gatekeepers of humanitarian aid and omits the democratic transition and free elections that Poland and the EU have demanded. We require explicit recognition of the National Assembly and interim President Juan Guaidó, unimpeded humanitarian access without political obstruction, and condemnation of violence against civilians and political prisoners. These are not technical amendments but conditions for Poland's support.
messages.South Africa: South Africa supports the draft as a balanced basis for the Council’s response. It rightly affirms sovereignty, non-interference and the need for a peaceful, Venezuelan-led political solution through dialogue, while encouraging humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles and the consent of the affected State. We therefore ask the penholder to retain this text and will support it in the vote.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support this text as drafted. It effectively legitimizes the Maduro regime, treats the crisis as purely internal, and conditions humanitarian access on the consent of authorities that have obstructed it. We need clear language on the illegitimate 2018 election, support for the National Assembly and interim President Guaidó, and unhindered humanitarian access. We will not support any text that fails to demand free and fair elections or that equates the Maduro regime with Venezuela's democratic opposition.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft as written: it legitimizes the illegitimate Maduro regime, conditions humanitarian aid on that regime's consent, and ignores the democratic transition led by Interim President Juan Guaidó. We require recognition of Guaidó and the National Assembly, removal of any language requiring coordination with Maduro for aid, condemnation of the regime's violence, and a clear call for free and fair elections. These are red lines for our delegation; the current text is unacceptable.

replies.Germany: partially accepted: added cross-border access, no political preconditions, elections, and general condemnation, but did not name security forces or include political prisoners.

replies.Peru: rejected: no recognition of Juan Guaidó, no condemnation of security forces, and no Lima Group reference.
replies.Poland: rejected: no recognition of Juan Guaidó, no removal of State consent, and no political prisoners language.
replies.South Africa: accepted: retained consent of the affected State and non-interference.

steps.summary: The revised text accommodates Côte d’Ivoire and Kuwait with elections in accordance with the Constitution, a National Assembly reference, and cross-border access while preserving Russian red lines on sovereignty, non-interference, and consent of the affected State. Western members remain opposed because the text does not recognize Juan Guaidó and retains State consent for humanitarian access. It is expected to receive 8 votes and be vetoed by Western permanent members.

messages.Belgium: Belgium welcomes the improvements on elections, the National Assembly, and humanitarian access, and can support the draft if the remaining humanitarian caveat is fixed. We cannot accept language that allows consent to be used to block aid; consent must not be withheld arbitrarily. We also ask that the text explicitly refer to international standards for elections, to the democratically elected National Assembly, and to violence against peaceful protesters and humanitarian personnel. With these changes Belgium is prepared to support; without them we would abstain.
messages.China: China supports the current text as circulated. It upholds sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in Venezuela’s internal affairs, and it promotes dialogue, restraint and humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles and the consent of the affected State. China appreciates the retention of these elements and sees no need for further changes. We support the draft as it stands.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire welcomes the penholder’s acceptance of our amendments on elections and humanitarian access. The current text strikes an appropriate balance by reaffirming Venezuela’s sovereignty and calling for a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led solution while addressing the humanitarian emergency. We can support the text as it stands and encourage all Council members to do the same.
messages.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic supports the draft’s emphasis on peaceful dialogue and humanitarian principles, but we cannot accept language that conditions aid on the consent of the de facto authorities or omits the legitimate National Assembly and its President. We request the changes above; if they are not reflected, we will abstain.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It upholds sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference and the consent and coordination of the affected State, while calling for peaceful dialogue without external interference. We therefore support the text as it stands and encourage all members to unite around it.
messages.France: France welcomes the inclusion of elections and the International Contact Group, but the current text remains unbalanced and could allow humanitarian access to be obstructed. Our red lines remain a clear call for free, fair and credible presidential elections without delay and for unhindered humanitarian access not subject to political conditions. We ask the penholder to reflect these changes; otherwise France cannot support the draft.
messages.Germany: Germany supports the humanitarian and dialogue elements, but the current text still falls short. We need explicit presidential elections with international observation, and we urge the Council to name excessive force by Venezuelan security forces and call for the release of political prisoners. Referring to the democratically elected National Assembly would also strengthen the text.
messages.Indonesia: Indonesia supports the draft as it stands. It reflects our position that the crisis must be resolved through peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led dialogue with full respect for sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference, and that humanitarian assistance must be neutral, impartial and coordinated with the United Nations and the affected State. We therefore request no amendments and encourage the Council to speak with one voice in support of dialogue, restraint and unhindered humanitarian access.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait thanks the penholder for incorporating its previous amendments, particularly on the National Assembly, land-border humanitarian access, and elections. The current text is balanced and reaffirms sovereignty, non-interference, and the need for a peaceful Venezuelan-led solution while addressing humanitarian access. Kuwait supports the text as it stands and is prepared to vote in favor.
messages.Peru: Peru cannot support this draft as it does not recognize the interim presidency of Juan Guaidó or the democratic legitimacy of the National Assembly, and it fails to condemn the Maduro security forces' violence. We reiterate our red-line amendments on recognition and humanitarian access, and ask that the Lima Group be reflected among regional efforts. Without these changes, Peru will vote against the text.
messages.Poland: Poland supports the draft’s humanitarian and dialogue objectives, but cannot support it as drafted because it effectively legitimizes the Maduro regime and makes humanitarian access conditional on its consent. We ask the penholder to include recognition of the National Assembly and interim President Guaidó, remove the State-consent language, and add clear language on political prisoners and accountability. Without these changes, Poland will vote against the text.
messages.South Africa: South Africa supports the revised draft. It reflects key principles we uphold: sovereignty, territorial integrity, non-interference, and the consent and coordination of the affected State for humanitarian assistance. We welcome the emphasis on peaceful and inclusive dialogue through regional mechanisms such as the Montevideo Mechanism and the International Contact Group, and we call on all Council members to support the text.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom cannot support the text as drafted: it perpetuates a false equivalence between the illegitimate Maduro regime and Venezuela's democratic institutions, and it conditions lifesaving humanitarian access on the consent of those obstructing it. We reiterate our red lines on recognizing the National Assembly and interim President Guaidó, removing the non-interference shield, and ensuring unhindered humanitarian access and credible elections. Without those core changes, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support a draft that treats the illegitimate Maduro regime as the legitimate authority, requires its consent for lifesaving aid, and fails to condemn its violence. We need the red-line changes above: recognition of Juan Guaidó and the National Assembly, unhindered humanitarian access without Maduro's consent, and accountability for the regime's repression. Without these, the United States will oppose the text.

replies.France: rejected: demands for presidential elections without delay and removal of consent undermine sovereignty and dialogue.
replies.Germany: partially accepted: general condemnation of violence against protesters added; attribution to security forces and demands for international observation rejected.
replies.Peru: rejected: recognition of Guaidó and Lima Group references are unacceptable and one-sided.

replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: rejected: demands to delete non-interference and recognize Guaidó are unacceptable.
replies.United States of America: rejected: demands to recognize Guaidó and remove consent interfere in Venezuela’s internal affairs.

steps.summary: The revised text preserves consent of the affected State, non-interference and the constitutional framework, while adding a general condemnation of violence against peaceful protesters and humanitarian personnel. Western red-line demands on recognizing Guaidó, removing consent and naming the Maduro government were rejected. The draft would likely receive 7 votes in favour, 5 against, including P5 negative votes, and 3 abstentions, and would therefore fail.

vetoed_by: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

reasons.Belgium: Belgium supports dialogue and humanitarian access but cannot back a Russian draft that rejects its red line on arbitrary consent for aid and weakens election and National Assembly language; abstention aligns with its balanced EU position.
reasons.China: China consistently upholds sovereignty, non-interference and peaceful settlement, and the Russian draft aligns with those principles, so China votes in favour. It speaks to explain its support for dialogue and neutral humanitarian action while opposing external intervention or escalation.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire had already signalled support for the Russian draft and it aligns with its emphasis on sovereignty, non-interference, peaceful dialogue and non-politicised humanitarian access. Its vote in favour also reflects a preference for a Venezuelan-led solution rather than external escalation.
reasons.Dominican Republic: The Dominican Republic historically abstained on the Russian draft; its key requested changes on humanitarian access and the National Assembly were not incorporated, making abstention consistent with its stated red lines and overall position.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea’s foreign policy consistently emphasizes sovereignty, non-interference and peaceful dialogue, and it had already indicated support for the Russian draft without requesting changes. The draft aligns with those priorities, so Equatorial Guinea votes in favour.
reasons.France: France opposed the Russian draft because its red-line amendments on immediate presidential elections and unimpeded humanitarian access were rejected, leaving language that could shield the Maduro government and block aid. This is consistent with France’s support for a Venezuelan-led democratic transition and the International Contact Group.
reasons.Germany: Germany’s red-line demand for presidential elections with international observation was rejected, and Berlin had recognized Juan Guaidó while insisting on unhindered humanitarian access. The Russian draft was therefore too weak on legitimacy and humanitarian access for Germany to support.
reasons.Indonesia: Indonesia’s established position favours non-interference, peaceful dialogue, and neutral humanitarian access, and its last negotiation position was support for this Russian-drafted text. Voting in favour with an explanation of vote protects those principles while opposing escalation or externally driven solutions.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait’s foreign policy emphasizes sovereignty, non-interference, and peaceful settlement, and the Russian draft aligns with those principles; Kuwait had already indicated support during negotiations. The draft’s calls for dialogue and humanitarian access provide sufficient basis for a favourable vote.
reasons.Peru: Peru aligned with the Lima Group, recognized Juan Guaidó, and had red-line demands on recognition and humanitarian access that the Russian draft rejected. Voting against is consistent with its stated position of opposing a text seen as legitimizing Maduro.
reasons.Poland: Poland’s red-line amendments recognizing Guaidó and ensuring unhindered humanitarian access without Maduro’s consent were rejected, and the Russian draft preserves a pro-Maduro framing; Warsaw therefore votes against.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor of the draft, Russia would vote in favour and use the pre-vote explanation to emphasize sovereignty, non-interference, and opposition to external intervention. This aligns with its established stance on Venezuela and its own submitted text.
reasons.South Africa: South Africa’s foreign policy prioritises non-interference, sovereignty, peaceful dialogue and opposition to external intervention; the Russian draft is consistent with these principles, and South Africa had already indicated support during negotiations.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The Russian draft rejected the UK’s red lines on recognizing Guaidó, rejecting non-interference as a shield, and ensuring unimpeded humanitarian access; the UK therefore votes against it.
reasons.United States of America: The United States recognized Juan Guaidó as interim president and viewed the Russian draft as shielding the Maduro government while omitting key US red lines on democratic legitimacy and humanitarian access. A negative US vote was therefore consistent with established policy and would constitute a veto.

before.Belgium: Mr. President, Belgium shares the concern of the Council at the grave humanitarian situation in Venezuela and remains committed to a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led political solution. We welcome the draft’s calls for restraint and respect for sovereignty, but we regret that the text does not adequately guarantee unhindered humanitarian access and does not sufficiently reflect the need for free and fair elections in accordance with international standards, nor the constitutional role of the democratically elected National Assembly. For these reasons, Belgium will abstain.
before.China:
Mr. President,

China supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation and will vote in favour. We believe that the situation in Venezuela should be resolved by the Venezuelan people themselves through inclusive political dialogue and negotiation, in accordance with Venezuela’s Constitution and laws. The purposes and principles of the UN Charter, especially sovereignty, independence, territorial integrity and non-interference in internal affairs, must be respected. China opposes the threat or use of force and external interference in Venezuela’s affairs. We support humanitarian assistance provided in accordance with the principles of humanity, neutrality, impartiality and independence and with the consent and coordination of the affected State, and we oppose the politicization of humanitarian aid. We also support the good offices of the Secretary-General and regional mediation efforts, including the Montevideo Mechanism and the International Contact Group, aimed at promoting a peaceful and inclusive solution. China believes that the Security Council should play a constructive role and avoid any action that could further escalate tensions.
before.Côte d’Ivoire: Mr. President, Côte d’Ivoire will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We do so because it reaffirms the sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela, and because it calls for a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led solution to the current crisis. Côte d’Ivoire is deeply concerned by the violence and loss of life, including at the country’s borders, and we urge all Venezuelan actors to exercise restraint, respect human rights and ensure safe, unhindered and impartial humanitarian access to those in need. We also encourage all political and social actors in Venezuela to engage in good faith dialogue and to work towards free, fair, transparent and credible elections in accordance with the Constitution and laws of Venezuela. Our vote is not a vote for any particular political actor; it is a vote for dialogue, restraint and the well-being of the Venezuelan people.
before.Dominican Republic: Mr. President, the Dominican Republic abstains. We remain deeply concerned by the deteriorating humanitarian situation and the loss of life in Venezuela. We supported the call for a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led dialogue and for the protection of civilians. However, we regret that the draft before us does not reflect the urgent need for immediate, unhindered and sustained humanitarian access without political conditions, nor does it recognize the role of the legitimately elected National Assembly or call for the release of political prisoners. For these reasons, we abstain. We urge all parties to refrain from violence and to engage in a credible process leading to free and fair elections, while fully respecting Venezuela's sovereignty and the principle of non-interference.
before.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support it because it reaffirms the sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity of Venezuela and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. It also calls for calm, the protection of civilians, and an inclusive political dialogue among Venezuelans, and it recalls that humanitarian assistance must be provided in accordance with humanitarian principles and with respect for the affected State. Equatorial Guinea urges all parties to refrain from violence and from any action that could further escalate tensions, and to pursue a peaceful, Venezuelan-led solution to the current crisis.
before.France: France cannot support this draft. The humanitarian emergency in Venezuela requires safe, unhindered and sustained access to those in need, without obstruction or political conditions. France has consistently called for a peaceful, Venezuelan-owned solution and for free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections without delay, leading to a democratic transition. Because the amendments that would have made these requirements clear were rejected, France will vote against this text.
before.Germany: Thank you, Mr. President. Germany shares the Council’s deep concern at the humanitarian emergency and the violence in Venezuela, and we support the calls for restraint and for humanitarian access. However, the draft before us does not meet the essential requirements for a credible political solution. It fails to call for free, fair, transparent and credible presidential elections with international observation, and it does not adequately uphold the legitimate and democratically elected National Assembly. It also risks making humanitarian assistance subject to the consent of authorities that have obstructed it. For these reasons, Germany will vote against this draft resolution.
before.Indonesia: Indonesia will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We continue to uphold the principles of sovereignty, political independence, territorial integrity and non-interference, and we believe that the situation in Venezuela must be resolved peacefully by Venezuelans themselves through inclusive dialogue and negotiation. We are deeply concerned by the violence and loss of life, including at the borders, and we call on all parties to exercise restraint and protect civilians. Humanitarian assistance must be neutral, impartial and independent, and must reach those in need without being politicised. Indonesia also supports the Secretary-General’s good offices and regional mediation efforts, and urges all States to avoid actions that could escalate tensions or undermine a peaceful settlement.
before.Kuwait: Thank you, Mr. President. Kuwait will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We remain deeply concerned by the humanitarian situation and the violence in Venezuela, and we believe that the only sustainable solution is a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led political process. Kuwait has consistently upheld the principles of sovereignty, territorial integrity and non-interference in the internal affairs of States, and we support dialogue among all Venezuelan actors, respect for the Constitution, and the avoidance of any use or threat of force. We also stress the need for safe and unhindered humanitarian access in accordance with humanitarian principles and in coordination with the affected State and impartial humanitarian actors. Kuwait therefore supports this balanced text and urges all parties to exercise restraint, protect civilians and work toward a peaceful settlement.
before.Peru: Peru will vote against this draft resolution. We fully support the search for a peaceful, democratic and Venezuelan-led solution and the unimpeded delivery of humanitarian assistance, but this text is unbalanced. It fails to recognize the interim presidency of Juan Guaidó and the democratic legitimacy of the National Assembly, and it would make humanitarian access conditional on the consent of authorities that are obstructing it. Peru cannot support a resolution that risks legitimizing an illegitimate regime and does not clearly condemn the grave human rights violations committed against the Venezuelan people. We call for free, fair and credible presidential elections without delay.
before.Poland: Mr President, Poland will vote against this draft resolution. We share the Council’s concern at the humanitarian situation and call for unhindered humanitarian access and accountability for violence, but this text remains unbalanced: it fails to recognize the democratically elected National Assembly and interim President Juan Guaidó, and it conditions humanitarian relief on the consent of the very de facto authorities obstructing it. Poland supports a peaceful, democratic and Venezuelan-led solution based on free and fair elections, respect for human rights, the restoration of legitimate institutions, and the immediate release of political prisoners.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation will vote in favour of the draft resolution it has submitted. The text is balanced and consistent with the Charter of the United Nations. It upholds the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of Venezuela and the principle of non-interference in internal affairs. It calls for peaceful and inclusive dialogue among Venezuelans and for humanitarian assistance to be provided in accordance with humanitarian principles and with the consent and coordination of the affected State. We reject any attempts to use humanitarian pretexts for political ends or external intervention, and we urge all States to refrain from actions that could further escalate tensions.
before.South Africa: Mr. President, South Africa will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We welcome its reaffirmation of the sovereignty, political independence, unity and territorial integrity of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela and of the principle of non-interference in the internal affairs of States. We also welcome its emphasis on a peaceful, inclusive and Venezuelan-led political solution through dialogue and negotiation, including the efforts of the Montevideo Mechanism and the International Contact Group, and on humanitarian assistance provided in accordance with humanitarian principles and in cooperation with the affected State. South Africa urges all Venezuelan actors to renounce violence, protect civilians, respect human rights and engage in good faith towards a durable political solution. We further urge all States to avoid actions that could exacerbate tensions, including external military intervention and unilateral coercive measures, and to support a peaceful settlement consistent with the Charter of the United Nations.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom votes against this draft resolution. We regret that the Council has before it a text that fails to reflect the reality of the crisis in Venezuela: the 20 May 2018 presidential election did not meet international standards, the National Assembly is the legitimate democratic institution in Venezuela, and the United Kingdom recognizes Juan Guaidó as interim President. We cannot accept language that invokes non-interference in internal affairs to shield human rights abuses, nor provisions that would subordinate humanitarian access to the consent of an illegitimate regime. The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by the humanitarian emergency, by the violence against peaceful protesters, and by the obstruction of aid. We call for unhindered humanitarian access, respect for human rights, and a peaceful, democratic, Venezuelan-led path forward, including free and fair presidential elections without further delay.
before.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States requests a vote and will vote against this draft. This text is not a neutral humanitarian appeal; it is an attempt to legitimize the illegitimate Maduro regime and to use the language of sovereignty to shield repression and block lifesaving assistance. It ignores the fraudulent May 2018 election, refuses to recognize Interim President Juan Guaidó and the democratically elected National Assembly, and fails to hold accountable those responsible for violence against peaceful protesters and humanitarian personnel. The United States supports the Venezuelan people and safe, unhindered humanitarian access leading to a peaceful democratic transition. We cannot support this resolution.

after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution it submitted because it was balanced, Charter-based and aimed at a peaceful, inclusive, Venezuelan-led solution. We regret that the Council could not adopt this text. The outcome shows that some members preferred to use the Council to promote a particular political outcome, to question Venezuela’s constitutional order and to legitimize external interference under humanitarian pretexts. The Russian Federation will continue to uphold the sovereignty, political independence and territorial integrity of Venezuela and the principle of non-interference in its internal affairs. Humanitarian assistance must be neutral and impartial and must be provided with the consent and coordination of the legitimate authorities. We call on all States to refrain from threats or the use of force, from steps that escalate tensions, and from any action that could undermine the peaceful settlement of the situation in Venezuela through dialogue, including the Montevideo Mechanism and other regional efforts. The rejection of this draft must not be used as a pretext for unilateral action or further destabilization.
after.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States is pleased that this draft was not adopted. It was never a genuine humanitarian text; it sought to legitimize the illegitimate Maduro regime and to use the language of sovereignty to shield repression and obstruct lifesaving assistance. The Council should have sent an unambiguous message in support of the Venezuelan people, Interim President Juan Guaidó, and the democratically elected National Assembly. The United States will continue to support safe, unhindered humanitarian access, a peaceful democratic transition, and free and fair elections in Venezuela. We will also continue to hold accountable those who obstruct humanitarian aid and commit violence against peaceful protesters. The Maduro regime must stop blocking assistance and respect the rights of the Venezuelan people. We urge all members of this Council to put the Venezuelan people first and to stand on the side of democracy, human rights, and the rule of law.
